# Single-vertex simplex cap lower bound and explicit stability

Historical claim of scope (pending review here): proved elementary simplex lemmas. These verify the middle-fiber estimates for the proposed small-third-fiber argument. They do not by themselves handle every ambient cut.

Let \(B\subset\mathbb R^d\) be a simplex, \(d\ge1\), of volume \(V>0\), with vertices \(v_1,\ldots,v_N\), where \(N=d+1\). Write \(\lambda_i\) for its barycentric coordinates and \(\gamma=(d/N)^d\).

## 1. Reused one-vertex cap formula

Accepted fact f75e1f526e17ab44 supplies the following input. For y in int(B) and affine f with f(y)=0, put alpha_j=f(v_j), assume alpha_i>0 and alpha_j<=0 for j!=i, and set t_j=alpha_i/(alpha_i-alpha_j). Then

    |B intersect {f>=0}|=V product_(j!=i)t_j,             (1)
    |B intersect {f>=0}|>=V d^d product_(j!=i)lambda_j(y). (2)

Equality is characterized by t_j=d lambda_j(y); it is attainable in this sign class exactly when lambda_j(y)<=1/d for j!=i. Boundary vertices are allowed. These facts are reused background. The submitted refinements are the explicit stable neighborhood and credit-dependent quadratic bound below.

## 2. A uniform neighborhood preserving the vertex sign pattern

Send \(B\) by a continuous affine transformation to the standard simplex. Its vertices and all its points have norm at most one. Suppose

\[
                 |\lambda_k(y)-1/N|\le\frac1{2N}
                 \qquad\text{for every }k.                \tag{3}
\]

Consider the through-point cut

\[
       \lambda_i(x)-\lambda_i(y)+v\cdot(x-y)\ge0,
                     \qquad |v|\le\frac1{8N}.             \tag{4}
\]

The perturbation at any vertex has magnitude at most \(2|v|\le1/(4N)\). At vertices \(j\ne i\), the unperturbed value is at most \(-1/(2N)\); at \(i\), it is at least
\(1-3/(2N)\ge1/(2N)\). Hence the margin in (4) is at least \(1/(4N)\) at \(i\), and at most \(-1/(4N)\) at every other vertex. In particular (2) applies with a strictly stable sign pattern.

Let \(n_i=\nabla\lambda_i\), and \(u_i=n_i/|n_i|\). Since \(1\le|n_i|\le\sqrt d\), every unit normal \(u\) satisfying

\[
                    |u-u_i|\le\frac1{8N\sqrt d}            \tag{5}
\]

is covered by (4), after positive rescaling by \(|n_i|\).

To combine this with `candidate 6b774d09877ca348`, take

\[
 \varepsilon_0=\min\left\{\frac{\delta}{24R},\frac1{8N}\right\},
       \qquad R=2\sqrt d,
       \qquad |u-u_i|\le\varepsilon_0/\sqrt d.             \tag{6}
\]

The middle sign pattern and the fixed endpoint credit then hold simultaneously, provided the respective center and mass conditions in that note hold.

## 3. The proposed credit-dependent point and a finite Taylor bound

Let fixed endpoint credits satisfy \(0\le c_i\le a\), and write
\(\bar c=N^{-1}\sum_i c_i\). Define

\[
              \lambda_i(y)=\frac1N+
                            \frac{c_i-\bar c}{N\gamma V}.
                                                               \tag{7}
\]

Put \(\eta=a/(\gamma V)\). If \(\eta\le1/2\), these coordinates sum to one, are strictly positive, and satisfy (3). Thus the point is well defined and the sign-stability neighborhood in (6) applies.

Set \(s_i=(c_i-\bar c)/(\gamma V)\). Then \(\sum_i s_i=0\), \(|s_i|\le\eta\), and

\[
        Vd^d\prod_{j\ne i}\lambda_j(y)
                     =\gamma V\prod_{j\ne i}(1+s_j).
\]

For \(\eta\le1\), expand the product. Its linear term is \(-s_i\), and the sum of absolute values of all terms of degree at least two is bounded by

\[
       \sum_{k=2}^d\binom dk\eta^k
              \le(2^d-d-1)\eta^2.
\]

Therefore the exact estimate is

\[
 \boxed{\quad
 Vd^d\prod_{j\ne i}\lambda_j(y)+c_i
 \ge\gamma V+\bar c-
          \frac{2^d-d-1}{\gamma}\frac{a^2}{V}.
 \quad}                                                     \tag{8}
\]

There is no unspecified remainder term. In dimension one the quadratic coefficient is zero and (8) is an equality.

If additionally \(\sum_i c_i\ge ja\), \(j=\lceil N/2\rceil\), then \(\bar c\ge ja/N\). For \(d\ge2\), set \(D_d=2^d-d-1>0\). Given any \(0\le\kappa<j/N\), the explicit smallness condition

\[
                \frac aV\le\frac{\gamma(j/N-\kappa)}{D_d}
                                                               \tag{9}
\]

makes the right side of (8) at least \(\gamma V+\kappa a\). In particular \(\kappa=\gamma/2\) is permitted in every dimension \(d\ge2\). This only proves the desired mass estimate for directions covered by the endpoint-credit neighborhood; the treatment of all remaining directions must still be supplied separately.

The exact algebra checks are in `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_simplex_single_vertex_cap_stability.py`.
